title: Medaka Kuroiwa Season 2 Heads to Crunchyroll in January 2027
description: Crunchyroll confirms a January 2027 stream of Medaka Kuroiwa Season 2 in North America, plus a December 6 preview at Anime Frontier in Texas.
keywords: Medaka Kuroiwa season 2, Crunchyroll January 2027, Anime Frontier Texas premiere, US anime streaming news
summary: The second season is confirmed for Crunchyroll in North America in January 2027. A preview screening is scheduled for December 6 at Anime Frontier in Fort Worth.
sections: What has been confirmed

Crunchyroll announced on November 11 that it will carry the second season of Medaka Kuroiwa Is Impervious to My Charms when the anime premieres in January 2027. The distributor explicitly lists North America among the streaming territories, which makes the announcement relevant to viewers in the United States. The announcement is about streaming rights and a premiere month; it is not yet an episode-by-episode release calendar.

Crunchyroll also confirmed a preview screening at Anime Frontier in Fort Worth, Texas, on December 6. That is a distinct event from the January streaming premiere. Attending a convention screening may require an event badge and could be subject to a separate schedule or capacity policy, so visitors should check the convention's official information before making travel plans.
Why this matters for US viewers

For fans who watched the first season, the most useful detail is distribution certainty. With North American rights announced, there is no need to rely on speculative regional listings to know the intended US streaming home. However, this does not establish the exact local release hour, the full subtitle-language lineup, or whether an English dub will arrive at the same time.

The series is a school-set romantic comedy, and the second season follows the first television run from January through March 2025. Fans following the original manga can also find an official English-language edition through Kodansha USA, as identified in Crunchyroll's announcement. The television anime and printed manga are separate products with different release schedules.
What to watch next

The three checkpoints are an official dated episode schedule, any English-dub announcement, and details of the December Texas screening. If a social post claims a precise January day or US streaming time before a platform announcement, treat that as unconfirmed. A confirmed premiere month is valuable news, but it is not the same as a confirmed minute-by-minute simulcast.

USA Anime Club has linked the source announcement below so readers can verify the geographic availability and convention detail directly. We will mark substantive changes with a new update date rather than silently changing the reported facts.

title: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend Sets February 2027 US Screenings
description: Crunchyroll and Sony announce February 21, 23 and 24 US screenings for Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend, with subtitle and dub options.
keywords: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend US release, February 2027 anime movie, Crunchyroll Sony Pictures theaters, anime film dub
summary: The anime film is scheduled for US theatrical screenings on February 21, 23 and 24, 2027, in both Japanese-with-English-subtitles and English-dub formats.
sourceLabel: Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures theatrical announcement, October 29, 2026
sections: The US dates and formats

Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures Entertainment have announced a limited set of North American screenings for Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend. The published schedule names February 21, 23 and 24, 2027, for theaters in the United States and Canada. The companies also listed Australia, where the release is scheduled for February 18.

US screenings are expected to offer both the original Japanese audio with English subtitles and an English-dub option. That distinction matters when choosing tickets: two screenings of the same film may use different audio formats. Theater availability, showtimes and format labels should be confirmed with the exhibitor before purchasing.
Where the film fits in the series

The film continues the Rascal Does Not Dream story rather than launching a standalone franchise. It follows earlier television and theatrical entries, so a first-time viewer may miss major character context by starting here. Crunchyroll's announcement lists the earlier series and films as part of its catalog at the time of publication, but licensing can change.

The movie debuted in Japanese theaters on October 16, 2026. Its US arrival in February 2027 is therefore a separate territorial theatrical release, not a new Japanese premiere. As is normal for limited anime screenings, a nationally announced date does not guarantee that every US market will have a participating cinema.
Practical booking checks

Before sharing a ticket listing, verify the film title, city, date and whether the screening is subtitled or dubbed. The announcement specifies three US dates; it does not establish ticket prices, the total number of screens or a future US streaming date. Those details should not be inferred from the theatrical notice.

For fans organizing a group visit, the most useful next step is to watch the official distributor's ticketing announcement and local theater listings. We will update this story when directly confirmed information becomes available, rather than treat unverified booking pages as final.

title: MASHLE Season 3 Confirmed for Crunchyroll Streaming in January 2027
description: The Tri-Magicathlon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc of MASHLE arrives in January 2027; Crunchyroll confirms US streaming rights.
keywords: MASHLE season 3 US streaming, Crunchyroll January 2027, Tri-Magicathlon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc, anime news
summary: Crunchyroll will stream MASHLE Season 3 during its January 2027 premiere window, with the United States included in the announced territories.
sections: Crunchyroll's distribution announcement

Crunchyroll confirmed on October 28 that MASHLE: MAGIC AND MUSCLES Season 3 will stream on the service beginning in January 2027. The new season carries the subtitle The Tri-Magicathlon Divine Visionary Final Exam Arc. The platform lists worldwide rights excluding Japan and China, which includes the United States.

That scope is unusually clear for a first licensing notice: American viewers can identify the announced destination without guessing whether the show will be available in their territory. The announcement stops short of publishing an exact American release time or a complete weekly episode calendar.
Returning production and story context

The new television season continues the adaptation produced at A-1 Pictures. According to the distributor, Tomonari Tanaka returns as director, with Yosuke Kuroda handling series composition and Masaru Yokoyama providing music. Chiaki Kozumi is named as the incoming character designer for the third season.

The show follows Mash Burnedead, a physically gifted student navigating a world where magical ability determines status. This installment advances the Divine Visionary examination storyline. The original manga by Hajime Komoto concluded in Japan in 2023; the official English edition is published by VIZ Media, independently of the anime streaming schedule.
What is not announced yet

The January window is confirmed, but readers should distinguish that from a confirmed exact date or same-day English dub. A streaming rights announcement also does not establish whether every audio language will launch together or whether episodes will be released simultaneously in all regions.

US fans can revisit the previous seasons on Crunchyroll while waiting for the platform's detailed winter schedule. For a release-time claim, check the show page or an official dated schedule rather than a countdown that cannot document its source.

title: Fall 2026 US Anime Lineup: Crunchyroll Confirms Black Clover and Apothecary Diaries

sections: Which returning shows are listed

Crunchyroll's official Fall 2026 seasonal lineup identifies Black Clover Season 2 and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 among its featured returning series. The distributor also lists Aoashi Season 2 and a larger slate of new premieres and continuing programs. Importantly for this publication, the lineup gives territorial information for individual shows rather than implying every series launches in every country.

The Black Clover listing names Studio Pierrot and a Saturday subtitled simulcast slot at 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time. The Apothecary Diaries listing names OLM and a Friday subtitled slot at 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time. These are the published slots from the lineup and can change; the source should be checked for subsequent updates.
Why the US catalog matters

North American availability is confirmed for both lead titles in the distributor's announcement. That is more useful to US readers than treating a global promotional poster as proof of local licensing. Distribution territory and language version are separate questions: a title may have a regional streaming home before a dubbed release schedule is finalized.

Crunchyroll's separate fall English-dub announcements provide additional context, but the exact status of a particular title should still be checked on its current show page. Platform catalogs, dates and language options are operational facts that may change after an initial announcement.
How to read an evolving seasonal schedule

The original fall slate was posted on September 15 and updated on October 6, 2026. A seasonal lineup is a living reference, not a permanent guarantee that every episode and audio option will appear at the originally printed minute.
